headline: Energy and Materials Lead Friday Advance as Tech Drag Keeps Gains in Check
body_html:
Stocks are broadly higher through midday Friday, with 325 names in our 544-stock universe trading up against 214 in the red. The session's dominant theme is a clear rotation toward commodity-linked and rate-sensitive groups: Energy is the top-performing sector, up 1.37%, followed by Homebuilders at 1.18% and Materials at 1.10%. Consumer names are adding a modest 0.71%, while Industrials trail at 0.46%.

The technology complex is the session's chief drag. Semiconductors are off 1.77% and Software is down 0.69%, weighed by sharp single-stock declines across power-module, identity-security, and cloud-monitoring names. Vicor Corporation is the session's worst performer, sliding 7.53%, while Twilio and Okta are each off more than 6%. The pressure in software and chips is keeping the broader tape from running harder despite constructive action elsewhere.

On the upside, Century Aluminum leads all gainers with a 4.46% advance, reinforcing the Materials bid. Dick's Sporting Goods follows at 4.18%, and Celsius Holdings adds 3.55%. Into the close, watch whether the tech selling intensifies or stabilizes — that dynamic, alongside weekend geopolitical headlines out of the Middle East, is likely to set the tone heading into Monday's open.

briefs.headline: Aluminum Shares Surge as Materials Sector Commands Friday Leadership
briefs.body: Century Aluminum has posted the session's largest gain, up 4.46% at midday, helping drive the Materials sector to a 1.10% advance. The move fits a broader Friday bid for commodity-exposed names, with Energy and Materials sitting atop the sector leaderboard as investors rotate away from growth-oriented technology positions.

briefs.headline: Software Stocks Face Broad Selling Pressure Across Multiple Subsectors
briefs.body: The Software sector is off 0.69% for the session, masking sharper moves in individual names. Twilio is down 6.59%, Okta is lower by 6.31%, and Datadog has shed 5.34% — declines spread across communications, identity-security, and cloud-monitoring categories, suggesting the selling is not isolated to a single catalyst.

briefs.headline: CoreWeave Fallout Casts Shadow Over AI-Adjacent Valuations
briefs.body: Markets are still processing the ripple effects of a CoreWeave sell-off, with analysts noting implications for valuations at competing AI infrastructure ventures. The wider Semiconductors sector is off 1.77% on the session, making it the weakest group in our universe and reflecting continued investor caution around AI-linked capital spending.

briefs.headline: Middle East Tensions Add Weekend Risk Premium to Friday Trade
briefs.body: Reports that the United States may consider striking an Iranian military site have introduced a geopolitical premium into Friday's session. Energy-services names are benefiting, with RPC Inc. and Innovex International each gaining more than 2.8%, as traders weigh potential supply-chain disruptions heading into a weekend of uncertain headlines.

briefs.headline: Homebuilders Post Second-Best Sector Performance Amid Rate Sensitivity Watch
briefs.body: The Homebuilder group is up 1.18% at midday, making it the second-best performing sector on the session. The advance reflects ongoing sensitivity to interest-rate expectations; any shift in Treasury market tone into the afternoon could test whether the group holds its gains through the close.

briefs.headline: Japanese Yen Policy Shift Noted as US Treasury Signals New Currency Stance
briefs.body: The US Treasury formally acknowledged that Japan is no longer operating in a deflationary environment and indicated that the yen's exchange rate warrants adjustment. The statement carries implications for currency markets and multinational earnings comparisons, a factor traders with international exposure will be monitoring into next week's open on Monday, October 19.
